subject: Acceptance of Ploop’s Offer
fact: After eating cooked fish and witnessing the rituals, the escapees, including Zalthir, accept Ploop’s offer to remain in Sloobludop and participate in the ritual exchange, abandoning their initial reluctance.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea.

subject: acceptance of Ploop’s offer
fact: The group, including Zalthir, accepts Ploop’s offer after witnessing their customs, eating cooked fish, and being reassured by Gloog’s honor-bound approach.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea... Zalthir is satisfied.

subject: Arrival at Sloobludop
fact: The escapees arrive at Sloobludop after an uneventful journey through tunnels. They are greeted by Kuo-toan sentinels who let them through the walls. They observe the village layout, the two altars, and the strange behaviors of the inhabitants. They are invited into Ploop’s quarters and begin to understand the religious conflict.
source_quote: They snap to attention when Ploop arrives and lets everyone through.

subject: arrival of the monitor and kuo-toa delegation
fact: Twelve kuo-toa led by a monitor arrive at Ploop’s quarters to escort him, his whip, and the prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: attempt to observe the Deep Father’s altar
fact: The escapees sneak to observe the altar of Leemooggoogoon but make noise, alerting the kuo-toans circling the idol and forcing a hasty retreat.
source_quote: Unfortunately, their attempt to be quiet is anything but. And the kuo-toans circling the Deep Father notice. 'I say we beat a hasty retreat,' whispers Thorin. 'These guys are spooky. Let’s get out of here,' mutters Zalthir.

One of our group got killed by another of our group. Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing."

subject: Bloppblippodd’s Cult
fact: Bloppblippodd leads a splinter faction that has abandoned the ways of the Sea Mother, embraced madness, and retains only a few hard-core supporters.
source_quote: Her hard-core supporters are few, but how many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown.

subject: Followers of Leemooggoogoon
fact: The followers of Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, worship a deity requiring blood sacrifices, preferably unwilling ones. Their idol is a stretched hide of a manta ray with pinned octopuses and a stained altar. They circle the idol in vigil and react violently to intrusions.
source_quote: She needs sacrifices for her false god. An unwilling sacrifice is better. This is an evil god.

subject: Followers of the Deep Father
fact: The followers of the Deep Father worship an idol of a manta ray made from hide, with pinned octopuses and a bloodstained altar. They demand unwilling sacrifices and are led by Bloppblippodd. Their numbers are uncertain, but they are a growing threat. Their practices are considered madness by Gloog and others.
source_quote: The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Followers of the Sea Mother
fact: The followers of the Sea Mother revere a scavenger goddess whose altar is adorned with severed crayfish parts, shells, mushrooms, and rotting fish. They believe the perfect offering is regurgitation. Ploopploopeen leads them, and they are the majority in the village. They are seen as traditionalists by Gloog.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Followers of the Sea Mother
fact: The followers of the Sea Mother worship a scavenger goddess who accepts regurgitated offerings. Their central idol is a wooden humanoid female adorned with the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed with gut and piled with shells, stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish. Four kuo-toans guard it constantly.
source_quote: The Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Kuo-toans
fact: The Kuo-toans are a society living between two walls of netting, with a cave wall to the south and the Darklake to the north. They sleep with eyes open, move in schools, and maintain order through designated leaders. Their religion centers on the Sea Mother and Leemooggoogoon, with rituals involving spit-offerings, blood sacrifices, and the use of severed body parts in idols.
source_quote: Many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Kuo-toan Society
fact: Kuo-toan society is fractured between followers of the Sea Mother and the Deep Father, with Bloppblippodd’s faction threatening collapse. The people sleep while standing, move in schools of fish, and revere idols made from severed body parts. Leadership is maintained by monitors who prevent madness from destroying social order. Rituals involve blood, rot, and unwilling sacrifices, and the existence of their gods is ambiguous.
source_quote: Many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: The Deep Mother's Followers
fact: The faction loyal to the Deep Mother, including Gloog and his allies, holds the support of the majority in the village and opposes the madness of Bloppblippodd’s followers.
source_quote: How many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown. This is why it must be dealt with now. While we still have the support of the majority.

subject: Altar of Leemooggoogoon
fact: The altar of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father consists of a large hide stretched between two poles in the shape of a manta ray, with a dead splayed-out manta ray pinned to its center, two dead octopuses draped across the top with tentacles pinned and heads tied together and painted red and blue, reeking of decay and stained dark with blood.
source_quote: They sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father. It consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles. A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide. Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments. The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Altar of the Deep Father
fact: The Altar of the Deep Father is a hide stretched between poles, shaped like a manta ray, with a dead manta ray pinned in the center and two dead octopuses draped across it. The altar is stained dark with blood and reeks of decay. It is surrounded by worshippers who chant and bow, and is guarded by a dozen followers of Bloppblippodd.
source_quote: The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Altar of the Sea Mother
fact: The Altar of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden statue of a humanoid female, with a severed giant albino crayfish head and claws lashed on with gut. It emits a powerful stench of rotting shellfish and is piled with shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish. It is guarded by four alert Kuo-toans and worshipped by many villagers.
source_quote: The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish.

subject: Altar of the Sea Mother
fact: The altar of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden statue of a humanoid female, with its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed on with gut strands and emitting a rotting shellfish stench, with shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish piled at its feet and strung around its neck.
source_quote: Ploop stops in front of the sizeable nine-foot-tall statue. The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish. Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: cave wall

subject: Darklake

source_quote: The Darklake side has docks. Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty.

subject: Darklake

source_quote: The Darklake side has docks. Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty. Walking along the docks are groups of Kuo-Toans.

subject: Ploop’s quarters

subject: Sea Mother's Altar
fact: The altar of the Sea Mother is a large wooden statue of a humanoid female, crudely carved and adorned with the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed with gut. Shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at its base and strung around its neck. It emits a powerful stench of rotting shellfish.
source_quote: The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish.

subject: Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is a Kuo-toan village with two concentric walls made of netting and stone, a cave wall to the south, and the Darklake to the north. The village lies between these barriers, with over a hundred mud-walled homes and ceilings made of unidentified dried vegetable matter. Docks line the Darklake, with some boats present. The town is dominated by two altars: one for the Sea Mother, one for the Deep Father.
source_quote: There are over a hundred houses of various sizes. Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.

subject: Derro
fact: Derro prisoners were previously captured and tied up by the party, an act noted by Gloog as both honorable and odd, implying a deeper cultural or moral context.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: Guardians of the Deep Father's Altar
fact: Kuo-toans circle the idol of Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, and immediately notice intruders. They are vigilant and hostile, triggering a confrontation when Grygum and others approach the altar.
source_quote: Unfortunately, their attempt to be quiet is anything but. And the kuo-toans circling the Deep Father notice.

subject: Guardians of the Sea Mother's Altar
fact: Four stern kuo-toans slowly circle the Sea Mother's altar, alert and on guard. They are part of the cult's permanent vigil and react to any disturbance near the idol.
source_quote: Four stern kuo-toa slowly circle the statue, alert and on guard...

subject: Kuo-toa
fact: Twelve kuo-toa accompanied their monitor to Ploopploopeen’s quarters as part of a formal escort mission to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters.

subject: Kuo-toa Monitor
fact: A kuo-toa monitor led twelve kuo-toa to Ploopploopeen’s quarters and was admitted by the archpriest of the Sea Mother to escort him, his whip, and the prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Kuo-toan Guardians
fact: Four stern Kuo-toans slowly circle the Sea Mother’s statue, alert and on guard. Others move about, bowing and chanting. They are not ordinary worshippers but specialized sentinels, likely trained to protect sacred sites. Their behavior is unnatural and deeply unsettling to the escapees.
source_quote: Four stern kuo-toa slowly circle the statue, alert and on guard, while a few others move about, gazing up at the statue and bowing repeatedly while chanting.

subject: Kuo-toan Monitor
fact: A Kuo-toan monitor arrives at Ploopploopeen’s quarters with twelve followers, signaling formal authority. Monitors are responsible for maintaining order and preventing societal collapse from madness. This monitor is acting on behalf of the Deep Father’s leadership and has come to escort the escapees to the altar of Leemooggoogoon.
source_quote: Twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is Gloog’s sister; she has been granted excessive deference by their father, has fallen prey to madness, and shows no respect for their society’s ways.
source_quote: Our society is torn to pieces by my sister Bloppblippodd. Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much. She has no respect for our ways. And she has fallen prey to this madness.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father and Ploopploopeen’s daughter, whose relationship with her father is strained and whose devotion to the Deep Father is questioned.
source_quote: My daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father and daughter of Ploopploopeen. She demands offerings for her deity and is the catalyst for the planned attack on the escapees. Her relationship with her father is troubled.
source_quote: In the morning, my daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father, Ploopploopeen’s daughter, who has fallen into madness and is seen as a threat to Kuo-toan society. She demands sacrifices for her false god, insists on unwilling offerings, and has amassed a faction of followers. Her relationship with her father is strained and unclear, and her existence as a legitimate cleric is questioned.
source_quote: She needs sacrifices for her false god.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an escapee who finds purpose in helping the Kuo-toans after a long history of running and loss. He is repulsed by the stench of the altars but pretends to be itchy to hide his discomfort. He is moved by the idea of having a goal after prison and death.
source_quote: Man, we've been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an escapee who finds purpose in helping the Kuo-toans after years of running and loss. He is repulsed by the stench of the Sea Mother’s altar but pretends it’s an itch. He shouts for food, is convinced by the promise of cooked fish, and sees the conflict as a meaningful end to their despair.
source_quote: Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, having escaped prison and witnessed the death of a group member, finds purpose in helping the Kuo-Toans and declares that having something to focus on is less depressing than running.
source_quote: Man, we’ve been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing. We busted out of prison, and then what? Ran. We’re being chased, and we keep running. One of our group got killed by another of our group. Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: Deep Father
fact: The Deep Father is the deity of Bloppblippodd, worshipped with a manta-ray hide idol and blood-stained altar, and is contrasted with the Sea Mother’s scavenger nature.
source_quote: The idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father... She has fallen prey to this madness.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg is known as Gloog to his friends; he disapproves of his father's decision to allow outsiders to meddle in their affairs, but acknowledges the party's respect for the Sea Mother and their understanding of their ways.
source_quote: Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg, called Gloog, is a Kuo-toan who disapproves of his sister Bloppblippodd’s rule and believes she has corrupted their traditions. He supports the escapees’ involvement in resolving the conflict, insists on honor-bound action without the first punch, and acknowledges the group’s respect for the Sea Mother. He is uncertain whether the escapees chose to spare the derro they captured.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg, who goes by Gloog, is a kuo-toan who disapproves of his sister Bloppblippodd’s actions and believes she has fallen prey to madness and disrespect for their ways.
source_quote: My name is Glooglugogg. Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways.

subject: Glooglugogg's Father
fact: Gloog’s father is the patriarch who has shown excessive deference to Bloppblippodd, enabling her descent into madness and fracturing their society.
source_quote: Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an escapee who recalls lore about the Deep Sea Mother and understands that regurgitation is a sacred offering. He spits on the altar, gains Ploop’s trust, and helps the group navigate Kuo-toan customs. He wonders what Ploop has heard and is aware of the ambiguity surrounding Leemooggoogoon’s existence.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is one of the escapees who begins to understand Kuo-toan rituals and misconceptions. He recognizes the altar of the Sea Mother as a scavenger deity and participates in the spit-offering. He is skeptical of Leemooggoogoon's existence and attempts to negotiate peace with symbols of parley.
source_quote: This is like a flag of parley. Have you considered a white flag?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is the perfect form of offering, and he spits on the altar to demonstrate respect.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering. Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understands that this is like a flag of parley.
source_quote: Grygum finally understands, "This is like a flag of parley."

subject: Kuo-toan monitor
fact: The kuo-toan monitor leads twelve kuo-toa to Ploopploopeen’s quarters and is admitted to oversee the transfer of prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Leemooggoogoon
fact: Leemooggoogoon is the Deep Father, a deity whose existence is questioned by Zalthir, worshipped by Bloppblippodd, and whose altar is marked by a manta-ray hide idol stained with blood.
source_quote: It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists... They sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother who has been ordered to accompany the monitor, his whip, and prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother who stares unblinkingly at the escapees and realizes the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen, the archpriest of the Sea Mother, stares unblinkingly at the escapees.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother, currently hosting the escapees in Sloobludop and attempting to broker a ritual exchange with the followers of Leemooggoogoon. He has strained relations with his daughter, Bloppblippodd, and is uncertain whether Leemooggoogoon actually exists.
source_quote: I will present you to her, and I will insist that I come with you. She will accept. And then all of my followers will attack.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother, who seeks to mediate between his people and outsiders, but struggles with communication and familial tension with his daughter Bloppblippodd. He believes offerings to the Sea Mother require regurgitation and spitting, and he is delighted when Grygum and Thorin comply. He sleeps standing and is observed walking outside while asleep.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen realizes that the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen realizes that the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says, "An unwilling sacrifice is better. This is an evil god."
source_quote: No. An unwilling sacrifice is better. This is an evil god.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says, "I tried that, but she didn’t bite. She needs sacrifices for her false god."
source_quote: I tried that, but she didn’t bite. She needs sacrifices for her false god.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says, "You will arrive in Sloobludop and stay in my quarters. I will send message to the followers of Leemooggoogoon that I have an offering for him. In the morning, my daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering. I will present you to her, and I will insist that I come with you. She will accept. And then all of my followers will attack. Your role in this will be over."
source_quote: No, this is wrong. You will arrive in Sloobludop and stay in my quarters. I will send message to the followers of Leemooggoogoon that I have an offering for him. In the morning, my daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering. I will present you to her, and I will insist that I come with you. She will accept. And then all of my followers will attack. Your role in this will be over.

subject: Sea Mother
fact: The Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess whose statue is made of wood and severed giant albino crayfish parts, and whose worship includes spitting and regurgitation as offerings.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar is referenced as having explained that the Kuo-Toans walking along the docks are leader types responsible for ensuring the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.
source_quote: These leader types that Shuushar explained are responsible for ensuring that the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an escapee who questions the effectiveness of Kuo-toan defenses and is wary of their food. He spits on the Sea Mother’s altar and is concerned about the nature of sacrifices. He is the first to suggest retreat when discovered at the Deep Father’s altar.
source_quote: I say we beat a hasty retreat.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an escapee who questions the effectiveness of Kuo-toan defenses, worries about food, and observes the unnatural behaviors of the Kuo-toans. He spits on the altar, is convinced by the promise of cooked fish, and later suggests retreat when the Deep Father’s altar is discovered.
source_quote: Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food, but Ploop... assures him that Kuo Toans eat cooked fish.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is wary of raw rotting food, questions the effectiveness of nEttin g walls, and participates in spitting on the Sea Mother’s altar.
source_quote: Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food... Thorin notes that the nEttin g isn’t an effective wall against a determined invader... Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Topsy and Turvy
fact: Topsy and Turvy are escapees who recognize the chaos of the situation as an opportunity for theft. They are not directly involved in ritual discussions but are attuned to the potential for looting.
source_quote: A free-for-all is an excellent opportunity to steal.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the party who seeks clarification on their role in the conflict; he is satisfied after learning they will assist without initiating violence.
source_quote: So when we go there, our job is just to sit around and do nothing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an escapee initially indifferent to the Kuo-toans' plight, seeing their conflicts as irrelevant. He is skeptical of their rituals but is eventually convinced by the promise of cooked fish and the group's acceptance of Ploop's offer.
source_quote: They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an escapee who initially sees no value in helping the Kuo-toans, questions his role repeatedly, and seeks clarity on whether he must fight. He is swayed by the promise of cooked food and the honor-bound nature of Gloog’s plan, and he is wary of the supernatural behaviors of the Kuo-toans.
source_quote: So when we go there, our job is just to sit around and do nothing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is skeptical of the Kuo-Toans’ cause, questions the existence of Leemooggoogoon, and initially sees no value in helping them until convinced by their customs.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders why they should bother. They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern... It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.

source_quote: the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood

source_quote: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: blood-stained stone altar

source_quote: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

source_quote: Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.

subject: Net Wall

subject: Sea Mother's Idol
fact: The idol of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden humanoid statue, its head and forearms composed of the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, bound with gut. It is decorated with brightly colored stones, mushrooms, shells, and rotting fish in garlands and piles.
source_quote: The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: Existence of Leemooggoogoon
fact: It is unclear whether Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, is a real deity or a construct used to justify ritual violence. Grygum and others suspect the god may not exist, but the cult’s fervor and the bloodstained altar suggest otherwise.

subject: Existence of Leemooggoogoon
fact: It is unclear whether Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, is a real deity or a delusion of Bloppblippodd’s. The escapees and even Gloog question the legitimacy of the god, and the rituals surrounding the idol may be the product of madness rather than faith.

subject: Kuo-toan Sleep Behavior
fact: Kuo-toans sleep while standing and move in schools of fish, suggesting they are not entirely human or are under supernatural influence. This behavior is normal to them but deeply disturbing to the escapees, and may hint at deeper magical corruption or transformation.
source_quote: Many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Purpose After Escape
fact: The escapees are searching for meaning after years of running, prison, and death. Daz’s declaration that having a purpose is less depressing than aimless flight resonates with the group, making them willing to engage in the kuo-toan conflict.
source_quote: Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: The Derro’s Fate
fact: The escapees captured a derro but chose not to hand them over to the Kuo-toans. Gloog finds this both honorable and odd, suggesting that the derro’s fate remains unresolved and may have consequences for future alliances or betrayals.
